title: Determinants: Minors, Cofactors, Adjoint, Inverse and Area
seo_title: Determinants Class 12 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 4)
standard_text: Determinant of a square matrix (up to 3 × 3 matrices), minors, co-factors and applications of determinants in finding the area of a triangle; adjoint and inverse of a square matrix; consistency, inconsistency and number of solutions of a system of linear equations by examples, solving a system of linear equations in two or three variables (having unique solution) using the inverse of a matrix (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 12 Determinants worksheet (NCERT Chapter 4): determinants of order 2 and 3, singular matrices, minors and cofactors, |kA|, adjoint and inverse, area of a triangle and the matrix method. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A⁻¹ = (1/|A|) adj A, which exists only when |A| ≠ 0.
key_sub: |kA| = kⁿ|A| and |adj A| = |A|ⁿ⁻¹ for an n × n matrix.
body_html:
How it works

  • |a b; c d| = ad − bc. Expand a 3 × 3 determinant along any row or column.
  • Minor Mij: delete row i and column j. Cofactor Aij = (−1)i+jMij.
  • adj A is the transpose of the matrix of cofactors; A(adj A) = |A| I; A−1 = adj A ÷ |A| when |A| ≠ 0.
  • Area of a triangle = ½|det| with rows (xi, yi, 1); the points are collinear when it is 0.
  • AX = B has the unique solution X = A−1B when |A| ≠ 0.
Example

Find |A| for A = [2 −3; 4 5].

ad − bc = 2 × 5 − (−3) × 4

= 10 + 12

Answer: 22

Common mistakes

  • Computing ad + bc instead of ad − bc.
  • Forgetting the sign (−1)^(i + j) in a cofactor.
  • Writing |3A| = 3|A| for a 3 × 3 matrix (it is 27|A|).
